scope: Theorem 1 (Parity lower bound) of the manuscript “Product-projection localization and the QAC0 parity lower bound” (preprints/Product-projection-localization-and-the-QAC0-parity-lower-bound-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 274 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 12393c9f997aa808), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 1. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a nonnegative integer d, a real number c ≥ 1, and 0 < ε ≤ 1/2. For all sufficiently large n, no circuit of depth at most d on n input qubits and at most nc total qubits, using arbitrary one-qubit unitaries and unbounded-arity Toffoli gates, computes PARITY(x) with probability at least 1/2 + ε for every x ∈ {0, 1}n. Gates in each layer have disjoint supports, ancillas start in |0⟩, and one output qubit is measured; the other qubits may be discarded.
